endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Tina Kotek for governor.
endorsements.excerpt: With deep ambivalence, we endorse Kotek for a second term.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Julia Brim-Edwards for Multnomah County chair (ranked #1).
endorsements.excerpt: Pragmatic and effective, she is Multnomah County’s best choice — and best chance — for righting the ship. Voters should rank Brim-Edwards as their number one candidate for chair.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Serena Cruz for Multnomah County Commissioner District 2 (ranked #1).
endorsements.excerpt: Voters should make the easy call and rank Cruz as their number one choice for the District 2 seat.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Pam Treece for Washington County chair.
endorsements.excerpt: Regardless of the distraction, however, voters’ choice is clear — they should elect Treece to put the county and the board of commissioners back on course.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Diane Sykes for Multnomah County circuit judge, Position 2.
endorsements.excerpt: But voters can pick only one. We recommend Sykes both for her breadth of experience and career-long dedication to protecting the rights of those least equipped to navigate the judicial system.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Joe Hagedorn for Multnomah County circuit judge, Position 14.
endorsements.excerpt: Considering the vast majority of people appearing in family court don’t have attorneys, the ability to calmly guide the parties through complicated situations is essential. The unanimous support from the other family-law judges in Multnomah County for Hagedorn also speaks to his readiness for the position.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Kellie Torres for Portland City Council District 3 (ranked #1).
endorsements.excerpt: Torres, 56, isn’t fazed by chaos or the lack of a roadmap. Instead, her work both inside and outside of Portland city government shows she brings the ingenuity and work ethic to find solutions for unsolved problems.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Steve Novick for Portland City Council District 3 (ranked #2).
endorsements.excerpt: Novick, 63, has proven his value to the City Council time and again.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Angelita Morillo for Portland City Council District 3 (ranked #3).
endorsements.excerpt: We strongly believe that. And of the DSA councilors and their allies on the City Council, no one is more effective in representing those views than Morillo.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Eric Zimmerman for Portland City Council District 4 (ranked #1).
endorsements.excerpt: Zimmerman, 41, is the councilor in the room who best demonstrates what a functional Council could look like.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Olivia Clark for Portland City Council District 4 (ranked #2).
endorsements.excerpt: Her actions show two things: Clark’s willingness to dive into Portland’s thorniest problems that others would sidestep and her courage to advance a solution that may be highly unpopular. District 4 should show their support for this essential work and rank Clark second on their ballot.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed Eli Arnold for Portland City Council District 4 (ranked #3).
endorsements.excerpt: Arnold, 46, was on our endorsement list in 2024, though he narrowly lost the final seat in the district to Zimmerman. We are once again endorsing him, ranking him third.

endorsements.statement: The Oregonian/OregonLive endorsed a no vote on Portland Measure 26-267 (participatory budgeting).
endorsements.excerpt: Portlanders already frustrated with high taxes and low levels of service should resist the calls to create another funding silo and vote “no” on Measure 26-267.

notes: Source text came from an RTF Prash pasted from oregonlive.com on 2026-10-18 (the site blocks our fetchers). Ranked-choice picks carry rank: Multnomah chair Brim-Edwards #1 only, County D2 Cruz #1 only ("rank Cruz as their number one choice"; the board endorses only Cruz), Council D3 Torres, Novick, Morillo and D4 Zimmerman, Clark, Arnold "in that order". Multnomah chair: Brim-Edwards #1 only ("Voters should rank Brim-Edwards as their number one candidate for chair"; "we are recommending only Brim-Edwards"); her article was pasted separately by Prash in the thread on 2026-10-18 (markdown links reduced to their text). Washington County chair = inventory race washington-county-commissioner-at-large (Treece vs Fai). Multnomah judge Pos. 2 and 14 = 4th District circuit court; "Joe Hagedorn" = Joseph Hagedorn, "Diane Sykes" = Diane S Sykes. Not endorsed (explicitly): Tiffany Koyama Lane (D3), Mitch Green (D4); other interviewed candidates mentioned without endorsement.
